property_summary: For any uint256 version, the oracle() address returned by atVersion(version) should be a contract (i.e., have code length > 0).
For any uint256 version, calling atVersion(version) must not revert.
For any uint256 version, the price returned by atVersion(version) should be non-negative (>= 0) as an integer.
For any uint256 version, the oracle address returned by atVersion().oracle should be the same as the contract's public getter oracle().
The oracle address returned by atVersion(uint256) must equal the contract's public oracle() getter.
The atVersion function returns the same price as the oracle's atVersion after applying the payoff definition transformation.
The atVersion function returns a price whose absolute value is greater than or equal to the raw oracle price's absolute value after applying a non-negative scaling factor.
The atVersion price equals the oracle's atVersion price transformed by the payoff definition.
The atVersion price is always the oracle's price transformed by the payoffDefinition's transform function (non-negative scaling).
The atVersion price is always the oracle's atVersion price transformed by the payoffDefinition's transform function.
For all oracle versions, the price returned by atVersion must be non-negative.
atVersion should succeed for version 0
The atVersion function always returns the same price regardless of the input version when the oracle returns a zero address.
The controller() function always returns a non-zero address according to the reference contract's controller() getter.
The controller() function always returns a non-zero address.
The maintenance fee returned by the public view function `maintenance()` must equal the value stored after initialization.
The public view function `maintenance()` must return the same value as the stored `_maintenance` value after initialization.
The maintenance value returned by maintenance() must be consistent between successive calls for the same product.
The maintenance() function must return a value that is unchanged after a sequence of two consecutive calls, unless an updateMaintenance() call was made.
The maintenance() function returns the same value as stored in the _maintenance storage after initialization, before any updateMaintenance call.
The funding fee returned by the contract is always a valid value (not zero) when the oracle version is non-zero.
The funding fee returned by the product is always greater than or equal to the controller's minimum funding fee.
The funding fee returned by the contract after any settlement is always equal to the contract's own stored funding fee value.
The atVersion oracle version returned always has the same price as the underlying oracle provider's atVersion price transformed by the payoff definition.
The funding fee returned by atVersion(uint256) before any settlement is always equal to the max of the product's stored fundingFee and the controller's minFundingFee.
makerFee() returns the same value when called within the same block (i.e., state-dependent view functions are pure functions of state).
When no one has updated the maker fee, calling makerFee() twice returns the same value.
The value returned by makerFee() is independent of the oracle version passed to atVersion().
makerFee() returns a value less than or equal to UFixed18.wrap(1e18) (i.e., 1.0 in fixed-point representation).
The value returned by makerFee() never changes after initialization, i.e., it is a constant function of the contract state (no pending updates or version-dependent changes).
makerFee must return a value <= 1e18 (i.e., not exceed 1).
makerFee must be less than or equal to the maximum possible fee of 1e18 (i.e., 100%).
Calling makerFee() returns the same value as the stored makerFee parameter after initialization.
After initialization, makerFee() returns a value less than or equal to the product's initial makerFee parameter.
If no fees have been updated, makerFee() must be less than 1e18.
For valid uint256 inputs, the makerFee() function should return the same value regardless of the input, and this value should match the stored maker fee.
The makerFee() function should always return the same value for any valid oracle version input, matching the stored maker fee.
For any valid oracle version input, the return value of makerFee() should equal the stored maker fee value set during initialization.
For any oracle version, the public makerFee() view function must return the stored maker fee value, not the stored taker fee.
The makerFee() function must never return a value that equals the takerFee() value.
For any input, makerFee() returns the same value as the stored _makerFee.read() (i.e., the product's maker fee parameter).
makerFee() returns the value stored in _makerFee.read()
makerFee() returns a value equal to maintenance() (since the mutant returns _maintenance.read() instead of _makerFee.read()).
The makerFee() function returns a value that remains unchanged after setting it via updateMakerFee(), provided the product has no pending positions.
For a valid maker fee update when there are no pending positions, the stored maker fee after the update equals the new value passed to updateMakerFee.
makerFee never returns the maximum UFixed18 value
makerFee returns a value less than or equal to UFixed18Lib.ONE
When makerFee is updated to a valid value, it never returns type(uint256).max.
The makerFee() function always returns a value that is less than or equal to UFixed18Lib.ONE.
The set of possible return values from makerFee() is a subset of the values less than or equal to UFixed18Lib.ONE.
takerFee always equals the value set by updateTakerFee, or zero when not yet set
takerFee always equals the value set by updateTakerFee, or zero when not yet set
After updateTakerFee(newFee), takerFee() must return newFee (ignoring zero default).
The `takerFee()` function must always return the value most recently set by `updateTakerFee()`, or a stale pending fee if a pending update exists, but never a constant zero.
The takerFee() function must not return zero after an updateTakerFee(nonZero) call completes successfully.
